title: Effectiveness of Generate–Verify–Repair with Deterministic Net-Specific Verifiers to Prevent Unsafe Configuration Changes
research_question: Does a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that uses an LLM to propose device-level network configuration changes and deterministic network-specific verifiers significantly reduce the rate of unsafe or policy-violating changes accepted for execution in a realistic NetOps sandbox compared with LLM-only proposals?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: LLM-only generated configuration proposals will accept a higher proportion of unsafe or policy-violating changes (when hypothetically applied) than proposals that pass a deterministic verifier.

H2: Interposing a deterministic verifier between generation and acceptance will reduce the proportion of proposals that would cause unsafe states by at least 50% relative to LLM-only (paired over tasks).

H3: A repair loop that re-invokes the LLM conditioned on deterministic verifier counterexamples (up to two repair iterations) will increase final verifier-pass rate relative to single-shot verification.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How does repair iteration count (0/1/2) marginally affect verifier pass probability across task types (routing, ACL, BGP)?
EQ2: What failure modes remain after GVR (reachability vs policy vs syntax), and do automated plausibility heuristics detect verifier-gaming cases?
benchmark_scope: Publicly seeded synthetic NetOps sandbox topologies (seeded topologies and traffic matrices described in preregistration).
Task types: device-level routing policy changes, ACL modifications, VLAN assignments, and BGP policy changes.
Scope explicitly bounded to deterministic-sandbox evaluation; no claims about production vendor-specific behavior beyond the modeled sandbox.
model_scope: Hosted LLM API(s) permitted by capability manifest (single-model primary scenario; optional second-model ensemble in extensive scenario).
Models used for generation only; deterministic verifiers and simulators are separate and not black-box models.
transformation_scope: Prompt-to-configuration generation (LLM outputs), automated canonicalization/parsing of config text to vendor-agnostic canonical form, deterministic verifier input transformations (Batfish-style JSON configs).
primary_estimand: Absolute and relative reduction (paired proportion) in 'unsafe-accepted' configuration proposals (would cause unsafe state if applied) for the GVR arm versus LLM-only across the 300 paired tasks.
secondary_estimands: Verifier-pass rate difference between LLM+verifier-gate and LLM-only.
Proportion of verifier-passed but sandbox-failure cases (verifier false-accept rate) estimated via deterministic sandbox simulation.
Effect of up-to-two repair iterations on final verifier pass probability (marginal benefit per iteration).
sampling_plan: Deterministic stratified sampling, total N=300 tasks, seed=2026-08-25. Task taxonomy: routing (150 tasks), ACL (100 tasks), BGP (50 tasks). Tasks drawn from public templates (published templates list included in preregistration artifact) with seeded random-number generator (seed above) and deterministic fault injection rules (link failures, route preference changes, missing ACL entries). Inclusion: tasks that map to device-level config patches. Exclusion: tasks requiring closed-source vendor features not representable in canonical form (deterministically filtered). All selection steps logged and hashed.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired-proportion (McNemar's exact) comparing 'unsafe-accepted' labels between LLM-only and (a) LLM+verifier-gate and (b) GVR (LLM+verify+repair). Report absolute risk reduction, relative risk reduction, and 95% exact binomial CIs. Use logistic regression (robust SE) to model verifier-pass as function of repair iteration count and task type for exploratory analysis. All tests two-sided; secondary tests adjusted using Benjamini–Hochberg to control false-discovery rate at 0.05. Predefined per-task pairing: each task receives outputs in all three arms under identical prompt seed to support within-task comparisons.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory comparisons are two paired contrasts vs LLM-only (verifier-gate and GVR). Secondary subgroup and iteration-count tests controlled with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR(0.05). All hypothesis-test families named in preregistration; p-values reported unadjusted and adjusted where applicable.
missingness_plan: Automatic exclusion rules: tasks with generation failures (no parseable config) are recorded as model-failure and excluded from paired hypothesis tests for that arm only; paired comparisons use only tasks with nonmissing paired outcomes. Missingness cause codes are logged; sensitivity analyses will impute worst-case and best-case outcomes for excluded items. No human adjudication: all exclusions and imputations are deterministically performed and logged.

risk_factors: Cross-run prompt leakage or dataset overlap between discovery and evaluation
Model call nondeterminism and vendor-API variability
detection_procedures: Hash-based provenance: all prompts, task templates, and seed lists hashed and timestamped; verify no pre-lock artifact hashes match evaluation artifacts.
Deterministic seeding for task selection and prompt variables to detect accidental reuse.
Output-duplicate detection: identical LLM outputs across tasks flagged deterministically.
item_flagging_rules: If any task template or config artifact hash matches a pre-lock development artifact hash, flag and exclude that task from confirmatory set.
If LLM outputs identical across arms for >10% of tasks (indicative of prompt leakage), trigger sensitivity analysis excluding duplicated items.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes flagged/contaminated tasks; sensitivity analyses report results including flagged tasks and report differences. All flagging is deterministic and automated; no human adjudication.
residual_uncertainty: Residual external-generalization risk to vendor-specific production environments
Possible verifier incompleteness for semantic failure modes not modelable in the sandbox

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended (balanced) — single hosted LLM, deterministic sandbox simulation, automated adversarial checks. Conservative expected average repair iterations = 1 for tasks requiring repair.
models: hosted-LLM-primary (single-model API permitted by capability manifest)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-task model calls: LLM-only=1, LLM+verifier=1, GVR average=2 (initial + avg 1 repair) => 4 calls/task * 300 = 1200. Fits capability manifest (max 10,000 calls) and estimated wall-clock budget.

budget_scenarios.description: Extensive — ensemble across two hosted LLM variants to test robustness to model choice; otherwise same pipeline; used for secondary robustness runs.
transformations: same as scenario SCEN-REC-1 applied per model (generation performed with both models)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-task calls per model (recommended-case average 4) * 2 models = 8 calls/task * 300 = 2400. Within maximum planned model-call budget and wall-clock constraints using hosted APIs.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired absolute reduction in proportion of unsafe-accepted proposals (GVR vs LLM-only) across N=300 paired tasks.
power_plan.target_effect: 50% relative reduction (e.g., from p0=0.30 to p1=0.15) in unsafe-accepted proportion.
power_plan.clustering_unit: Task (each task paired across three arms).
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate McNemar/paired-proportion power calc: with N=300 and baseline p0=0.30, paired design detects a reduction to 0.15 (relative 50% reduction) with two-sided alpha=0.05 and power > 0.8 under conservative discordance assumptions. Exact calculation details and code included in preregistration artifact.
assumptions: Baseline unsafe-accepted proportion under LLM-only p0 assumed 0.30 (conservative prior; sensitivity analyses will report alternative baselines 0.20 and 0.40).
Discordant-pair rates consistent with McNemar assumptions; paired design reduces between-task variance.
Effective N=300 after automatic deterministic exclusions (exclusions logged and sensitivity-analysed).
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=300, the minimum detectable absolute reduction is ~0.075–0.10 (7.5–10 percentage points) depending on discordant-pair distribution; this supports detecting the preregistered 50% relative reduction under the baseline assumptions.
sensitivity_analyses: Power recalculation for baseline p0 in {0.2,0.3,0.4}.
Recompute primary test excluding flagged/contaminated tasks and with worst-case imputed outcomes for excluded items.

transformation_families: Config text -> parsed vendor-agnostic canonical representation
semantic_equivalence_checks: Automated parsing and canonicalization: configs pass syntax parse and canonical form equality checks (AST-equivalence) before verifier ingestion.
Behavioral equivalence check in sandbox: canonicalized config applied to deterministic simulator to confirm intended change semantics.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject LLM outputs failing vendor-agnostic parser (syntax errors) automatically; record as model-failure.
Reject configs with ambiguous interface references (deterministically flagged by name-resolution rules).
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated deep-simulation audit on deterministic 10% stratified sample per task type (no human review). Audit runs include exhaustive reachability checks and additional traffic scenarios to estimate verifier false-accept rates.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Intent-to-config mapping is validated by (1) deterministic template coverage tests, (2) parser roundtrip checks (generate -> parse -> regenerate canonical form), and (3) automated sandbox behavioral simulation verifying intended policy change.
residual_risks: Verifier incompleteness for semantic classes not representable in the sandbox.
LLM may produce superficial repairs that exploit verifier assumptions (deterministically detected via adversarial heuristics but not perfectly eliminated).

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Deterministic verifier and sandbox model incompleteness for vendor-specific proprietary behaviors (bounded: claims limited to synthetic sandbox).

Risk of LLM producing superficial 'verifier-gaming' repairs yielding verifier passes but semantic issues undetectable by current sandbox checks (mitigated but not eliminated by automated adversarial heuristics and audit sampling).
External-generalization: results on the synthetic/public sandbox may not fully transfer to production networks with proprietary features or unseen topologies.
